en: 'Abdullah ibn al-Rumi al-Yamami, 'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-'Azim al-'Anbari, and Ahmad ibn Ja'far al-Ma'qiri narrated to us, they said: Al-Nadr ibn Muhammad narrated to us, 'Ikrimah—who is Ibn 'Ammar—narrated to us, Abu al-Najashi narrated to us: Rafi' ibn Khadij narrated to me, he said: The Prophet of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) came to Medina while they were pollinating the date palms—saying: they were fecundating the date palms. He said: "What are you doing?" They said: "We used to do it." He said: "Perhaps if you did not do it, it would be better." So they abandoned it, and it shed its unripe dates or yielded less—he said—so they mentioned that to him, whereupon he said: "I am only a human being. When I command you with something regarding your religion, adhere to it; but when I command you with something from my personal opinion, then I am only a human being." 'Ikrimah said: Or something similar to this. Al-Ma'qiri said: "and it shed its unripe dates," without doubt.

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id al-Thaqafi and Abu Kamil al-Jahdari narrated to us—and their wordings were close, this being the narration of Qutaybah—they said: Abu 'Awanah narrated to us, from Simak, from Musa ibn Talhah, from his father, he said: I passed with the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) by some people atop date palms. He said: "What are these people doing?" They said: "They are pollinating them, putting the male part into the female part so that it becomes pollinated." The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "I do not think that avails anything." He said: So they were informed of that and abandoned it. The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) was then informed of that, so he said: "If that benefits them, let them do it, for I only assumed an assumption, so do not hold me to an assumption. But when I narrate something to you from Allah, adhere to it, for I will never lie about Allah, Mighty and Majestic."

'Abdullah ibn Barrad al-Ash'ari and Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' al-Hamdani narrated to us, they said: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Burayd, from Abu Burdah, from Abu Musa, he said: The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) was asked about things he disliked. When they persisted in asking him, he became angry, then said to the people: "Ask me about whatever you wish." A man said: "Who is my father?" He said: "Your father is Hudhafah." Another arose and said: "Who is my father, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Your father is Salim, the freed slave of Shaybah." When 'Umar saw the anger on the face of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), he said: "O Messenger of Allah, indeed we repent to Allah." And in the narration of Abu Kurayb: He said: "Who is my father, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Your father is Salim, the freed slave of Shaybah."

Yahya ibn Habib al-Harithi narrated to us, Khalid—meaning Ibn al-Harith—narrated to us; (H) and Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us, both from Hisham; (H) and 'Asim ibn al-Nadr al-Taymi narrated to us, Mu'tamir narrated to us, he said: I heard my father; all of them said: Qatadah narrated to us, from Anas, with this story.

Yusuf ibn Hammad al-Ma'ni narrated to us, 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, that the people questioned the Prophet of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) until they pressed him excessively with questioning. So he came out one day, ascended the pulpit, and said: "Ask me! You will not ask me about anything except that I will make it clear to you." When the people heard that, they fell silent in awe and feared that something grave was imminent. Anas said: I began looking right and left, and behold, every man had wrapped his head in his garment, weeping. Then a man from the mosque who used to be disputed with and called after someone other than his father rose and said: "O Prophet of Allah, who is my father?" He said: "Your father is Hudhafah." Then 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) spoke up and said: "We are pleased with Allah as Lord, with Islam as religion, and with Muhammad as Messenger, seeking refuge with Allah from the evil of trials." The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "I have never seen the like of today in good and evil! Paradise and Hell were depicted to me, and I saw both of them on this side of the wall."

'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us, 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, Ma'mar informed us; (H) and 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Darimi narrated to us, Abu al-Yaman informed us, Shu'ayb informed us, both from al-Zuhri, from Anas, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) with this hadith and the hadith of 'Ubaydullah with it, except that Shu'ayb said: from al-Zuhri: 'Ubaydullah ibn 'Abdullah informed me, he said: A man from the people of knowledge narrated to me that the mother of 'Abdullah ibn Hudhafah said... with the like of the hadith of Yunus.

Harmalah ibn Yahya ibn 'Abdullah ibn Harmalah ibn 'Imran al-Tujibi narrated to me, Ibn Wahb informed us, Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab: Anas ibn Malik informed me that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) came out when the sun passed its meridian and led them in the Zuhr prayer. When he concluded the prayer with peace, he stood upon the pulpit and mentioned the Hour, and mentioned that preceding it are momentous matters. Then he said: "Whoever wishes to ask me about anything, let him ask me about it; for by Allah, you will not ask me about anything except that I will inform you of it as long as I am in this standing place of mine." Anas ibn Malik said: The people wept profusely when they heard that from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), while the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) kept repeating: "Ask me!" Thereupon 'Abdullah ibn Hudhafah arose and said: "Who is my father, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Your father is Hudhafah." As the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) kept saying, "Ask me," 'Umar fell to his knees and said: "We are pleased with Allah as Lord, with Islam as religion, and with Muhammad as Messenger." He said: So the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) fell silent when 'Umar said that. Then the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Woe! By the One in Whose Hand is the soul of Muhammad, Paradise and Hell were just presented before me in the direction of this wall, and I have never seen the like of today in good and evil." Ibn Shihab said: 'Ubaydullah ibn 'Abdullah ibn 'Utbah informed me, he said: The mother of 'Abdullah ibn Hudhafah said to 'Abdullah ibn Hudhafah: "I have never heard of a son more undutiful than you! Were you safe from the possibility that your mother might have committed some of what the women of the pre-Islamic period of ignorance committed, thereby disgracing her in the sight of the people?" 'Abdullah ibn Hudhafah said: "By Allah, even if he had affiliated me with a black slave, I would have accepted his affiliation!"

Muhammad ibn Ma'mar ibn Rib'i al-Qaysi narrated to us, Rawh ibn 'Ubadah narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us: Musa ibn Anas informed me, he said: I heard Anas ibn Malik saying: A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, who is my father?" He said: "Your father is so-and-so." And there was revealed: {O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if they are shown to you, will distress you} to the end of the verse.

Mahmud ibn Ghaylan, Muhammad ibn Qudamah al-Sulami, and Yahya ibn Muhammad al-Lu'lu'i narrated to us—and their wordings are close; Mahmud said: Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl narrated to us, and the other two said: Al-Nadr informed us—Shu'bah informed us, Musa ibn Anas narrated to us, from Anas ibn Malik, he said: Something reached the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) regarding his Companions, so he delivered a sermon and said: "Paradise and Hell were displayed to me, and I have never seen the like of today in good and evil. If you only knew what I know, you would laugh little and weep much." He said: No day was harder upon the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) than that day. He said: They covered their heads, sniffling with tears. He said: 'Umar arose and said: "We are pleased with Allah as Lord, with Islam as religion, and with Muhammad as Prophet." He said: Then that man arose and said: "Who is my father?" He said: "Your father is so-and-so." Thereupon there was revealed: {O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if they are shown to you, will distress you}.

And Harmalah ibn Yahya narrated it to me, Ibn Wahb informed us, Yunus informed me; (H) and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us, 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, Ma'mar informed us, both from al-Zuhri, with this chain of transmission. And in the hadith of Ma'mar he added: "a man who asked about something and probed deeply into it." And in the hadith of Yunus he said: from 'Amir ibn Sa'd that he heard Sa'd.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated it to us, they said: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from al-Zuhri; (H) and Muhammad ibn 'Abbad narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, he said: "I remember it just as I remember: In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful"—al-Zuhri from 'Amir ibn Sa'd, from his father, he said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "The greatest sinner among Muslims regarding the Muslims is the one who asked about a matter that had not been made forbidden, but it was made forbidden for the people on account of his questioning."

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Sa'd informed us, from Ibn Shihab, from 'Amir ibn Sa'd, from his father, he said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Indeed, the greatest sinner among the Muslims regarding the Muslims is the one who asked about something that was not forbidden to the Muslims, but it was made forbidden to them on account of his questioning."

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Layth narrated to us; (H) and Muhammad ibn Rumh narrated to us, al-Layth informed us, from Ibn Shihab, from 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, that 'Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr narrated to him that an Ansari man disputed with al-Zubayr before the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) concerning the irrigation streams of the Harrah with which they watered date palms. The Ansari said: "Let the water pass through." But he refused him, so they disputed before the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace). The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said to al-Zubayr: "Irrigate, O Zubayr, then release the water to your neighbor." The Ansari became angry and said: "O Messenger of Allah, is it because he is the son of your paternal aunt?" Thereupon the color of the face of the Prophet of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) changed, and he then said: "O Zubayr, irrigate and then retain the water until it rises to the walls." Al-Zubayr said: "By Allah, I think that this verse was revealed concerning that: {But no, by your Lord, they will not believe until they make you judge in what is disputed between them and then find within themselves no discomfort}."

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Muslim, from Masruq, from 'A'ishah, she said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) granted a concession in a matter, but some of the people abstained from it. That reached the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and he became angry until anger showed on his face, then he said: "What is the matter with people who shun what has been permitted to me? By Allah, I am the most knowledgeable of them concerning Allah, and the most intensely fearful of Him among them."

Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, Hafs—meaning Ibn Ghiyath—narrated to us; (H) and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim and 'Ali ibn Khashram narrated it to us, they said: 'Isa ibn Yunus informed us, both of them from al-A'mash, with the chain of transmission of Jarir, similar to his hadith.

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us, Jarir narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, from 'A'ishah, she said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) did something and took a concession in it, and that reached some of his Companions, so they seemed to dislike it and abstained from it. That reached him, so he stood up to deliver a sermon and said: "What is the matter with men who, having heard of a matter I took a concession in, dislike it and abstain from it? By Allah, I am the most knowledgeable of them concerning Allah, and the most intensely fearful of Him among them."

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Hanzali narrated to us, Jarir informed us, from al-A'mash, from 'Amr ibn Murrah, from Abu 'Ubaydah, from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, he said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) used to name for us several of his names, so he said: "I am Muhammad, Ahmad, al-Muqaffi (the Last Follower of Prophets), al-Hashir (the Gatherer), the Prophet of Repentance, and the Prophet of Mercy."

'Abd al-Malik ibn Shu'ayb ibn al-Layth narrated to me, he said: My father narrated to me, from my grandfather: 'Uqayl narrated to me; (H) and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us, 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, Ma'mar informed us; (H) and 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Darimi narrated to us, Abu al-Yaman informed us, Shu'ayb informed us, all of them from al-Zuhri, with this chain of transmission. And in the hadith of Shu'ayb and Ma'mar: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)." And in the hadith of 'Uqayl, he said: I said to al-Zuhri: "And what is al-'Aqib?" He said: "The one after whom there is no prophet." And in the hadith of Ma'mar and 'Uqayl: "the disbelievers." And in the hadith of Shu'ayb: "disbelief."

Harmalah ibn Yahya narrated to me, Ibn Wahb informed us, Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, from Muhammad ibn Jubayr ibn Mut'im, from his father, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Indeed, I have names: I am Muhammad, I am Ahmad, I am al-Mahi (the Eraser) through whom Allah erases disbelief, I am al-Hashir (the Gatherer) at whose feet people will be gathered, and I am al-'Aqib (the Final Successor) after whom there is no one." And Allah indeed named him compassionate and merciful.

Zuhayr ibn Harb, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, and Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to me—and the wording is Zuhayr's; Ishaq said: informed us, while the other two said: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us—from al-Zuhri: he heard Muhammad ibn Jubayr ibn Mut'im, from his father, that the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "I am Muhammad, I am Ahmad, I am al-Mahi (the Eraser) through whom disbelief is erased, I am al-Hashir (the Gatherer) at whose heels people will be gathered, and I am al-'Aqib (the Final Successor)." And al-'Aqib is the one after whom there is no prophet.

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Hanzali narrated to us, Rawh informed us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from 'Ammar ibn Abi 'Ammar, from Ibn 'Abbas, he said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) stayed in Mecca for fifteen years: hearing the voice and seeing the light for seven years without seeing any tangible form, and for eight years receiving revelation, and he stayed in Medina for ten years.
And Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from Khalid, with this chain of transmission.

Nasr ibn 'Ali narrated to me, Bishr—meaning Ibn Mufaddal—narrated to us, Khalid al-Hadhdha' narrated to us, 'Ammar, the freed slave of Banu Hashim, narrated to us: Ibn 'Abbas narrated to us that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) passed away when he was sixty-five years old.
Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to me, Shababah ibn Sawwar narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Yunus, with this chain of transmission, similar to the hadith of Yazid ibn Zuray'.

Ibn Minhal al-Darir narrated to me, Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us, Yunus ibn 'Ubayd narrated to us, from 'Ammar, the freed slave of Banu Hashim, he said: I asked Ibn 'Abbas: "How old was the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) on the day he died?" He said: "I did not think that someone like you among his people would not know that." He said: I said: "I have asked the people and they differed with me, so I wished to know your view on it." He said: "Can you count?" He said: I said: "Yes." He said: "Hold forty, at which he was sent (with prophethood), fifteen in Mecca experiencing safety and fear, and ten from his emigration to Medina."

Ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us—and the wording is Ibn al-Muthanna's—they said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us: I heard Abu Ishaq narrating from 'Amir ibn Sa'd al-Bajali, from Jarir, that he heard Mu'awiyah delivering a sermon, wherein he said: "The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) died when he was sixty-three years old, as did Abu Bakr and 'Umar, and I am sixty-three years old."

'Abdullah ibn 'Umar ibn Muhammad ibn Aban al-Ju'fi narrated to us, Sallam Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, he said: I was sitting with 'Abdullah ibn 'Utbah when they mentioned the years of the Messenger of Allah's (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) age. Some of the people said: "Abu Bakr was older than the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)." 'Abdullah said: "The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) passed away when he was sixty-three years old, Abu Bakr died when he was sixty-three years old, and 'Umar was killed when he was sixty-three years old." He said: Then a man among the people called 'Amir ibn Sa'd said: Jarir narrated to us, he said: We were sitting with Mu'awiyah when they mentioned the years of the Messenger of Allah's (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) age. Mu'awiyah said: "The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) passed away when he was sixty-three years old, Abu Bakr died when he was sixty-three years old, and 'Umar was killed when he was sixty-three years old."

Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us, Bishr ibn al-Sari narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, from Abu Jamrah al-Duba'i, from Ibn 'Abbas, he said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) remained in Mecca for thirteen years receiving revelation, and in Medina for ten years, and he died when he was sixty-three years old.

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim and Harun ibn 'Abdullah narrated to us, from Rawh ibn 'Ubadah: Zakariyya ibn Ishaq narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from Ibn 'Abbas, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) remained in Mecca for thirteen years and passed away when he was sixty-three years old.

Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Amr, he said: I said to 'Urwah: "How long did the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) stay in Mecca?" He said: "Ten years." I said: "Indeed Ibn 'Abbas says: thirteen to nineteen (a dozen or so years)." He said: "He sought forgiveness for him," and said: "He only took that from the words of a poet."
